name: uses every digit in the no-bound minimum
input: digits containing zeros with and without nonzero digits
test:
assert smallest_number([4, 1, 4, 2, 3]) == '12344'
assert smallest_number([0, 2, 5]) == '205'
assert smallest_number([0, 0]) == '0'

name: returns the mathematically smallest valid bounded permutation
input: an exact bound, a former contradictory example, and a shorter bound
test:
assert smallest_number([6, 2, 9], 629) == '629'
assert smallest_number([1, 6, 4], 300) == '416'
assert smallest_number([1, 2, 3, 3, 4], 332) == '12334'

name: handles leading zeros, duplicates, and bound length boundaries
input: shorter and longer bounds plus all-zero inputs
test:
assert smallest_number([0, 0, 4], 20) == '400'
assert smallest_number([1, 2], 30) == '-1'
assert smallest_number([0, 0], 0) == '0'
assert smallest_number([0, 0], 1) == '-1'
